sentences.text: Brief facts of the present case are that the marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized according to Hindu rites and ceremonies in Delhi.
It is stated that the marriage was duly consummated and a child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is further stated that since 2016, respondent no. 2 left her matrimonial home and came back to her parental home situated at Fazalpur, Delhi and the parties started residing separately.
It is further stated that respondent no. 2 had filed an application under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. before the Court of learned Principal Judge, Family Court, East Delhi, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Court, East Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is further stated that respondent no. 2 had filed a complaint before Crime Against Women Cell, Delhi against the petitioners, which finally culminated into the said FIR.
It is further submitted that the charge sheet has been filed against the present petitioners and now the trial is at the stage of framing of charges.
It is stated that both the parties mutually agreed to settle their disputes and wanted to end their marital relationship.
Accordingly, a settlement agreement dated 25.11.2023 was drawn and accepted by both the parties.
It is stated that the divorce was granted to the parties on 13.02.2024.
In view of the settlement and divorce granted to the parties, the present petition has been filed.
6. All the parties are present before this Court in-person and have been identified by their counsel and Investigating Officer concerned.

7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/06/2024 at 22:51:12 threat.
It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide settlement agreement dated 25.11.2023.
It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has already received the remaining amount of Rs. 5,00,000/-.

This Courts attention has been also invited to the Settlement Agreement, paragraph 9 specifically, where it is mentioned that the rights of the minor child will not be affected.
8.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.
9. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received all amounts due to her and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

10. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter,
This Court is of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
